50	// HandleListWikiPages returns all wiki pages for a project
51	func (s *Server) HandleListWikiPages(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
52		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 5*time.Second)
53		defer cancel()
54	
55		userID := r.Context().Value(UserIDKey).(int64)
56		projectID, err := strconv.ParseInt(chi.URLParam(r, "projectId"), 10, 64)
57		if err != nil {
58			respondError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid project ID", "invalid_input")
59			return
60		}
61	
62		// Verify user has access to this project
63		hasAccess, err := s.checkProjectAccess(ctx, userID, projectID)
64		if err != nil {
65			respondError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to verify project access", "internal_error")
66			return
67		}
68		if !hasAccess {
69			respondError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "access denied", "forbidden")
70			return
71		}
72	
73		// Fetch all wiki pages for the project
74		pages, err := s.db.Client.WikiPage.Query().
75			Where(wikipage.ProjectID(projectID)).
76			WithCreator().
77			WithUpdater().
78			Order(ent.Asc(wikipage.FieldTitle)).
79			All(ctx)
80		if err != nil {
81			s.logger.Error("Failed to fetch wiki pages",
82				zap.Int64("project_id", projectID),
83				zap.Error(err),
84			)
85			respondError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to fetch wiki pages", "internal_error")
86			return
87		}
88	
89		// Bulk-fetch agent_name (not in Ent schema) for all pages in this project
90		agentNames := make(map[int64]*string)
91		if len(pages) > 0 {
92			rows, qErr := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT id, agent_name FROM wiki_pages WHERE project_id = $1`, projectID)
93			if qErr == nil {
94				defer rows.Close()
95				for rows.Next() {
96					var id int64
97					var an *string
98					if scanErr := rows.Scan(&id, &an); scanErr == nil && an != nil {
99						agentNames[id] = an
100					}
101				}
102			}
103		}
104	
105		// Convert to response format
106		response := make([]WikiPageResponse, 0, len(pages))
107		for _, p := range pages {
108			wp := WikiPageResponse{
109				ID:        p.ID,
110				ProjectID: p.ProjectID,
111				Title:     p.Title,
112				Slug:      p.Slug,
113				CreatedBy: p.CreatedBy,
114				UpdatedBy: p.UpdatedBy,
115				CreatedAt: p.CreatedAt,
116				UpdatedAt: p.UpdatedAt,
117			}
118			if p.Edges.Creator != nil && p.Edges.Creator.Name != nil {
119				wp.CreatorName = p.Edges.Creator.Name
120			}
121			if p.Edges.Updater != nil && p.Edges.Updater.Name != nil {
122				wp.UpdaterName = p.Edges.Updater.Name
123			}
124			if an, ok := agentNames[p.ID]; ok {
125				wp.AgentName = an
126			}
127			response = append(response, wp)
128		}
129	
130		respondJSON(w, http.StatusOK, response)
131	}

133	// generateSlug creates a URL-friendly slug from a title
134	func generateSlug(title string) string {
135		// Convert to lowercase
136		slug := strings.ToLower(title)
137		// Replace spaces and special chars with hyphens
138		reg := regexp.MustCompile("[^a-z0-9]+")
139		slug = reg.ReplaceAllString(slug, "-")
140		// Remove leading/trailing hyphens
141		slug = strings.Trim(slug, "-")
142		// Truncate to max 100 chars
143		if len(slug) > 100 {
144			slug = slug[:100]
145		}
146		return slug
147	}

557	// maybeCreateVersion creates a version snapshot if versioning criteria are met.
558	func (s *Server) maybeCreateVersion(ctx context.Context, pageID, userID int64, newContent string, manualSave bool, agentName *string) error {
559		hash := fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256([]byte(newContent)))
560	
561		// Fetch last version
562		lastVersion, err := s.db.Client.WikiPageVersion.Query().
563			Where(wikipageversion.WikiPageID(pageID)).
564			Order(ent.Desc(wikipageversion.FieldVersionNumber)).
565			First(ctx)
566		if err != nil && !ent.IsNotFound(err) {
567			return err
568		}
569	
570		// Skip if content identical to last version
571		if lastVersion != nil && lastVersion.ContentHash == hash {
572			return nil
573		}
574	
575		shouldVersion := manualSave
576		if !shouldVersion {
577			if lastVersion == nil {
578				// First content — version it
579				if newContent != "" {
580					shouldVersion = true
581				}
582			} else if time.Since(lastVersion.CreatedAt) > 15*time.Minute {
583				// Time-based snapshot
584				shouldVersion = true
585			} else if isSignificantChange(lastVersion.Content, newContent) {
586				// Large diff
587				shouldVersion = true
588			}
589		}
590	
591		if !shouldVersion {
592			return nil
593		}
594	
595		versionNum := 1
596		if lastVersion != nil {
597			versionNum = lastVersion.VersionNumber + 1
598		}
599	
600		ver, err := s.db.Client.WikiPageVersion.Create().
601			SetWikiPageID(pageID).
602			SetVersionNumber(versionNum).
603			SetContent(newContent).
604			SetContentHash(hash).
605			SetCreatedBy(userID).
606			Save(ctx)
607		if err != nil {
608			return err
609		}
610	
611		// Set agent_name via raw SQL (Ent schema doesn't have this field yet)
612		if agentName != nil {
613			if _, execErr := s.db.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE wiki_page_versions SET agent_name = $1 WHERE id = $2`, *agentName, ver.ID); execErr != nil {
614				s.logger.Warn("Failed to set agent_name on wiki version", zap.Error(execErr), zap.Int64("version_id", ver.ID))
615			}
616		}
617		return nil
618	}
619	
620	// isSignificantChange returns true when the diff is >15% of old or >500 chars changed.
621	func isSignificantChange(oldContent, newContent string) bool {
622		oldLines := strings.Split(oldContent, "\n")
623		newLines := strings.Split(newContent, "\n")
624	
625		oldSet := make(map[string]int, len(oldLines))
626		for _, l := range oldLines {
627			oldSet[l]++
628		}
629	
630		charsChanged := 0
631		for _, l := range newLines {
632			if oldSet[l] > 0 {
633				oldSet[l]--
634			} else {
635				charsChanged += len(l)
636			}
637		}
638		// Also count lines removed from old
639		for l, cnt := range oldSet {
640			charsChanged += len(l) * cnt
641		}
642	
643		if charsChanged > 500 {
644			return true
645		}
646		if len(oldContent) > 0 && float64(charsChanged) > 0.15*float64(len(oldContent)) {
647			return true
648		}
649		return false
650	}

832			Where(

863				zap.Int64("page_id", pageID),

866		}

872		})

65		defer s.emailMu.Unlock()
66		s.emailService = nil
67	}

69	// GetEmailService returns the email service, loading from DB if needed. Returns nil if not configured.
70	func (s *Server) GetEmailService() *email.BrevoService {
71		s.emailMu.RLock()
72		if s.emailService != nil {
73			svc := s.emailService
74			s.emailMu.RUnlock()
75			return svc
76		}
77		s.emailMu.RUnlock()
78	
79		// Load from DB
80		s.emailMu.Lock()
81		defer s.emailMu.Unlock()
82	
83		// Double-check after acquiring write lock
84		if s.emailService != nil {
85			return s.emailService
86		}
87	
88		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
89		defer cancel()
90	
91		var apiKey, senderEmail, senderName, status string
92		err := s.db.QueryRowContext(ctx,
93			`SELECT api_key, sender_email, sender_name, status FROM email_provider WHERE id = 1`,
94		).Scan(&apiKey, &senderEmail, &senderName, &status)
95		if err != nil {
96			return nil
97		}
98	
99		if status == "suspended" {
100			return nil
101		}
102	
103		s.emailService = email.NewBrevoService(apiKey, senderEmail, senderName, s.logger)
104		return s.emailService
105	}

# Build stage — runs on host arch, cross-compiles via GOARCH
# Uses modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go) so CGO is not needed
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.26-alpine AS builder

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git

WORKDIR /build

# Copy go mod files
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Get version information
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG GIT_COMMIT=unknown
ARG BUILD_TIME=unknown
ARG TARGETARCH

# Build static binary — no CGO needed (modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go)
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=${TARGETARCH} go build \
    -ldflags="-w -s \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.Version=${VERSION}' \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.GitCommit=${GIT_COMMIT}' \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.BuildTime=${BUILD_TIME}'" \
    -o taskai \
    ./cmd/api

# Production stage
FROM alpine:3.19

# Install CA certificates, pg_dump (for backup), and create non-root user
RUN apk --no-cache add ca-certificates tzdata postgresql-client && \
    addgroup -g 1001 -S taskai && \
    adduser -u 1001 -S taskai -G taskai

# Create data directory with correct permissions
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown taskai:taskai /data

WORKDIR /app

# Copy binary from builder
COPY --from=builder --chown=taskai:taskai /build/taskai .

# Copy OpenAPI spec (needed for /api/openapi endpoint)
COPY --chown=taskai:taskai openapi.yaml .

# Copy database migrations
COPY --chown=taskai:taskai internal/db/migrations ./internal/db/migrations

# Switch to non-root user
USER taskai

# Expose port
EXPOSE 8080

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8080/api/health || exit 1

# Run the binary
CMD ["./taskai"]

// Import generated types from OpenAPI spec
import type { components, operations } from './api.types'

// Re-export types for convenience
export type User = components['schemas']['User']
export type AuthResponse = components['schemas']['AuthResponse']
export type SignupRequest = components['schemas']['SignupRequest']
export type LoginRequest = components['schemas']['LoginRequest']
export type Project = components['schemas']['Project']
export type Task = components['schemas']['Task'] & { task_number?: number; github_issue_number?: number | null; github_repo?: string; start_date?: string | null; github_reactions?: GitHubReaction[]; agent_name?: string | null }
export type ApiError = components['schemas']['Error']

export interface GitHubReaction {
  reaction: string
  count: number
  user_reacted?: boolean
}

// Types with required fields for commonly used API responses
export interface TaskComment {
  id: number
  task_id: number
  user_id: number
  user_name?: string | null
  agent_name?: string | null
  comment: string
  created_at: string
  updated_at: string
  github_reactions?: GitHubReaction[]
}

export interface ActivityEntry {
  id: number
  project_id: number
  user_id: number
  user_name?: string
  action: string
  entity_type: string
  entity_id: number
  entity_title?: string
  details?: Record<string, unknown>
  created_at: string
}

export interface Sprint {
  id: number
  user_id: number
  name: string
  start_date?: string
  end_date?: string

# Build stage — runs on host arch, cross-compiles via GOARCH
# Uses modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go) so CGO is not needed
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.26-alpine AS builder

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git

WORKDIR /build

# Copy go mod files
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Get version information
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG GIT_COMMIT=unknown
ARG BUILD_TIME=unknown
ARG TARGETARCH

# Build static binary — no CGO needed (modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go)
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=${TARGETARCH} go build \
    -ldflags="-w -s \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.Version=${VERSION}' \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.GitCommit=${GIT_COMMIT}' \
      -X 'taskai/internal/version.BuildTime=${BUILD_TIME}'" \
    -o taskai \
    ./cmd/api

# Production stage
FROM alpine:3.19

# Install CA certificates, pg_dump (for backup), and create non-root user
RUN apk --no-cache add ca-certificates tzdata postgresql-client && \
    addgroup -g 1001 -S taskai && \
    adduser -u 1001 -S taskai -G taskai

# Create data directory with correct permissions
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown taskai:taskai /data

WORKDIR /app

# Copy binary from builder
COPY --from=builder --chown=taskai:taskai /build/taskai .

# Copy OpenAPI spec (needed for /api/openapi endpoint)
COPY --chown=taskai:taskai openapi.yaml .

# Copy database migrations
COPY --chown=taskai:taskai internal/db/migrations ./internal/db/migrations

# Switch to non-root user
USER taskai

# Expose port
EXPOSE 8080

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8080/api/health || exit 1

# Run the binary
CMD ["./taskai"]

All builds pass. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

---

## Wiki Download Feature

### API Endpoints (auth required)
- **`GET /api/wiki/pages/{pageId}/pdf`** — Generates and downloads PDF that matches web rendering
- **`GET /api/wiki/pages/{pageId}/markdown`** — Downloads raw markdown file

### Backend (`api/internal/api/wiki_download_handler.go`)
- PDF generation uses **chromedp** (headless Chromium) with inlined CSS that replicates the Tailwind Typography `prose` styles in light mode (better for print)
- Same markdown→HTML pipeline as the preview endpoint (go-wiki + graph links + figma shortcodes)
- Markdown download serves raw content with `Content-Disposition: attachment`
- Shared `fetchWikiPageWithAccess()` helper for access control
- Dockerfile updated to install `chromium` package

### MCP Tools
- **`download_wiki_pdf`** — Returns base64-encoded PDF with filename
- **`download_wiki_markdown`** — Returns raw markdown content with filename

### Frontend (WikiEditor.tsx)
- Download dropdown button (arrow-down icon) between version history and fullscreen buttons
- Two options: "Download PDF" and "Download Markdown"
- Loading states while PDF generates (can take a moment due to headless Chrome)
- Click-outside-to-close behavior

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `api/internal/api/wiki_download_handler.go` | New — PDF + markdown download handlers |

| `api/go.mod` / `api/go.sum` | Added `chromedp` dependency |

| `mcp/src/api.ts` | `getWikiPagePdf()` + `getWikiPageMarkdown()` |

## 1. Current Data Model — Assets, Scans & Backups (catalog DB)

[draw:ubrjqlqzdy:edit:m]

### Core Tables

**`catalog.assets`** — The central entity. Every protected resource (EC2, EBS, S3, EFS, OVA server, Azure VM/disk/blob, IBM COS, FSx ONTAP) is an asset. Partitioned by `tenant_name`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | Internal identifier |
| `tenant_name` | varchar | Tenant partition key |
| `account_id` | varchar | AWS account / Azure subscription |
| `region` | varchar | Cloud region |
| `cc_asset_id` | varchar | Cloud Connector asset ID |
| `resource_name` | varchar | Human-readable name |
| `kind` | varchar | `ec2_instance`, `ebs_volume`, `s3_bucket`, `efs_filesystem`, `generic_host`, `ova_server`, `fsx_ontap_volume`, `azure_storage_blob_container`, `azure_compute_disk`, `azure_compute_vm`, `ibm_cos_bucket`, `azure_storage_file_share` |
| `tags` | jsonb | Cloud resource tags |

**`catalog.asset_health`** — Derived health state per asset. The `health_state` column is a **generated column**: `infected` if any threat counts > 0, `clean` if malware + ransomware scans exist and no threats, otherwise `at_risk`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `asset_id` | uuid PK | FK → assets |
| `malware_threat_count` | int | Active malware threats |
| `ransomware_threat_count` | int | Active ransomware threats |
| `filesystem_error_threat_count` | int | FS integrity issues |
| `encryption_threat_count` | int | Encryption issues |
| `latest_*_scan` | timestamptz | Last scan timestamp per kind |
| `health_state` | enum | **GENERATED**: `infected` / `clean` / `at_risk` |

**`catalog.backups`** — Recovery points. Linked to assets via `source_asset_id`. Each backup tracks its scan status across all four check types.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `source_asset_id` | uuid FK | → assets.id |
| `provider` | varchar | `aws`, `elastio`, `ova_veeam`, `azure_*`, etc. |
| `kind` | varchar | 24 backup kinds (elastio_aws_ec2, awsb_s3, aws_ebs_snapshot, ova_*, azure_*, etc.) |
| `fs_check_status` | varchar | `not_applicable` / `unchecked` / `good` / `bad` |
| `ransomware_check_status` | varchar | Same enum |
| `malware_check_status` | varchar | Same enum |
| `encryption_check_status` | varchar | Same enum |

**`catalog.scans`** — Individual scan executions against targets (assets or backups).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `target` | jsonb | Contains `asset_id` or `resource.asset_id` |
| `kind` | varchar | `malware_scan`, `ransomware_scan`, `fs_check`, `entropy_scan` |
| `status` | varchar | `good` / `bad` |
| `type` | varchar | `direct` (live asset) / `backup` (recovery point scan) |

**`catalog.threats`** — Detected threats linked to scans and backups.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `kind` | varchar | `malware`, `ransomware`, `filesystem_error`, `encryption` |
| `status` | varchar | `detected`, `resolved`, `ignored` |
| `backup_ids` | uuid[] | Affected backups |
| `detected_by_scan_ids` | uuid[] | Scans that found this threat |

**`catalog.scan_threat_relation`** — M:N join table between scans and threats.

**`catalog.anomalies`** — High-entropy file detections (potential ransomware indicators). Currently only `kind = 'high_entropy_files'`.

### Relationships

```
Asset (1) ──→ (1) Asset Health
Asset (1) ──→ (N) Backups        (via source_asset_id)
Asset (1) ──→ (N) Scans          (via target jsonb → asset_id)
Scan  (N) ←──→ (M) Threats       (via scan_threat_relation)
Threat(1) ──→ (N) Backups        (via backup_ids array)
```

---

## 2. Policy Data Model (pechkin DB)

[draw:puqk8tzivd:edit:m]

Policies live in the **pechkin** database, separate from the catalog. They define *what* gets backed up, *how often*, and *with what scan settings*.

### Core Tables

**`pechkin.policies`** — The operational policy definition. PK is `(tenant_name, name)`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `name` | varchar PK | Policy name (unique per tenant) |
| `frequency` | jsonb | Cron-like schedule definition |
| `status` | varchar | `enabled` / `disabled` / `paused_until` |
| `selectors` | jsonb[] | Asset selection rules (by tag, kind, etc.) |
| `account_region_selectors` | jsonb[] | Scope to specific accounts/regions |
| `iscan` | jsonb | Scan configuration (which scan types to run) |
| `kind` | varchar | `default` / `custom` |
| `vaults` | jsonb[] | Target vault configuration |
| `mode` | jsonb | `{"kind_tag": "backup"}` or scan-only |
| `integrity_check` | varchar | `disabled` / `file_system` |
| `protect_new_immediately` | varchar | Auto-protect new matching assets |
| `platform` | varchar | Currently only `AWS` |

**`pechkin.plans`** — Mirror of policies used by the backup scheduler. Nearly identical schema to policies, used for execution planning.

**`pechkin.backup_windows`** — Scheduled time windows for policy execution.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `policy_name` | varchar FK | → policies.name |
| `start_at` / `end_at` | timestamptz | Window boundaries |
| `is_finalized` | bool | Whether all assets in window are processed |

**`pechkin.backup_window_assets`** — Assets scheduled within a specific backup window. Links individual assets to their execution status within a window.

**`pechkin.backup_plan_coverage`** — Tracks which assets (by red_stack_asset_id) are covered by which plan, per red_stack.

### How Policies Connect to Assets

Policies don't directly FK to assets. Instead:
1. **Selectors** (`selectors` jsonb[]) define rules that match assets by tags, kind, or name patterns
2. **Account/Region selectors** further scope which cloud accounts and regions are included
3. At execution time, matching assets are materialized into **backup_window_assets** records
4. The **backup_plan_coverage** table caches which assets each plan covers per red_stack

This means an asset's policy association (visible in the UI as "Policy: -" or "Policy: MyPolicy") is derived at query time by matching the asset against policy selectors, not stored as a direct FK.

---

## 3. Posture Attributes — Proposed Data Model

[draw:m35vd4hjw4:edit:m]

Posture is a **new concept** that aggregates security and compliance signals into a holistic view of each asset's protection stance. Unlike the current health model (which is purely threat-based), posture considers:

- **Backup coverage** — Is the asset covered by a policy? How stale is the last backup?
- **Scan coverage** — Are all scan types running? When was the last scan?
- **Encryption status** — Are backups encrypted?
- **Policy compliance** — Does the asset meet its policy's requirements?

### Proposed Tables

**`asset_posture`** — Per-asset posture evaluation. Computed periodically or on-demand.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `tenant_name` | varchar PK | Partition key |
| `asset_id` | uuid PK | FK → catalog.assets |
| `backup_coverage` | enum | `covered` / `partial` / `uncovered` |
| `last_backup_age_hours` | int | Hours since last successful backup |
| `policy_name` | varchar | Associated policy (nullable if uncovered) |
| `scan_coverage` | enum | `full` / `partial` / `none` |
| `last_scan_at` | timestamptz | Most recent scan of any kind |
| `encryption_status` | enum | `encrypted` / `unencrypted` / `mixed` |
| `compliance_score` | float | 0–100 composite score |
| `evaluated_at` | timestamptz | When this posture was last computed |

**`posture_rules`** — Configurable rules that define what "good posture" means for a tenant.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `name` | varchar | Human-readable rule name |
| `rule_type` | enum | `backup_frequency`, `scan_coverage`, `encryption`, `retention`, `recovery` |
| `condition` | jsonb | Rule logic (e.g., `{"max_backup_age_hours": 24}`) |
| `severity` | enum | `critical` / `high` / `medium` / `low` |
| `enabled` | bool | Toggle rules on/off |

**`posture_violations`** — When an asset fails a posture rule, a violation is recorded.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | uuid PK | |
| `asset_id` | uuid FK | → catalog.assets |
| `rule_id` | uuid FK | → posture_rules |
| `status` | enum | `open` / `resolved` / `suppressed` |
| `detected_at` | timestamptz | When violation was first detected |
| `resolved_at` | timestamptz | When auto-resolved (nullable) |
| `details` | jsonb | Context (e.g., actual vs expected backup age) |

**`posture_snapshots`** — Tenant-level aggregate snapshots for trend dashboards.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `tenant_name` | varchar PK | |
| `snapshotted_at` | timestamptz PK | Point-in-time |
| `total_assets` | int | |
| `covered_assets` | int | Assets with active policy |
| `compliant_assets` | int | Assets with score ≥ threshold |
| `avg_compliance_score` | float | Tenant-wide average |
| `violation_counts` | jsonb | Breakdown by severity/rule_type |

### How Posture Interacts with Existing Models

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    POSTURE LAYER                    │
│                                                     │
│  asset_posture ←── reads from:                      │
│    • catalog.assets          (asset existence)      │
│    • catalog.asset_health    (threat state)          │
│    • catalog.backups         (backup recency)        │
│    • catalog.scans           (scan coverage)         │
│    • pechkin.policies        (policy association)     │
│    • pechkin.backup_windows  (schedule compliance)   │
│                                                     │
│  posture_rules ──→ posture_violations               │
│    Evaluated against asset_posture                  │
│                                                     │
│  posture_snapshots                                  │
│    Aggregated from asset_posture + violations       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key design decisions:**

1. **Posture is read-only / computed** — it does not modify existing tables. It reads from catalog + pechkin and materializes a posture view.
2. **Decoupled from health** — `health_state` (infected/clean/at_risk) is a threat signal. Posture is a compliance/coverage signal. An asset can be `clean` (no threats) but have `poor posture` (no policy, stale backups).
3. **Rules are tenant-configurable** — Different tenants can define different thresholds for what constitutes acceptable backup frequency, scan coverage, etc.
4. **Violations auto-resolve** — When the underlying condition is fixed (e.g., a backup runs), the violation is automatically marked resolved.
5. **Snapshots enable trending** — The `posture_snapshots` table enables "posture over time" dashboards without querying the full violation history.

### Where should posture tables live?

Two options:
- **In catalog DB** — Natural fit since posture is primarily about assets. Keeps the read path simple.
- **In a new `posture` DB** — Cleaner separation of concerns, avoids adding new concepts to an already large catalog schema.

Recommendation: **catalog DB**, since posture queries will frequently join with assets, backups, and scans. A separate DB would require cross-database joins or data duplication.","updated_at":"2026-04-17T20:12:56.095036Z"}

- Pixel-perfect output matching the web rendering exactly

content.text: The deploy is running. The new approach: 1. For each `[draw:ID]` in the wiki page, chromedp navigates to `http://localhost:8080/draw/{ID}?theme=light` (the actual canvas viewer) 2. Waits for the canvas to render 3. Takes a PNG screenshot of just the `` element 4. Embeds the screenshot as a base64 data URI `` in the PDF HTML 5. Then prints the final HTML to PDF This means the diagrams in the PDF will look **exactly** like what you see when viewing the drawing in your browser — same text wrapping, same layout, same everything. For the blog at aiagentlens.com — the SVG export endpoint (`/draw/{id}/export.svg`) also got the multiline text fix in v0.9.15, so those should improve too. But since the blog likely uses the SVG directly (not chromedp screenshots), the rendering won't be perfectly identical to the canvas — it's close but not pixel-perfect. If you want pixel-perfect blog images too, we could add a PNG export endpoint to go-draw using the same screenshot approach.

1	package images
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"net/http"
8		"os"
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/aws"
12		"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials"
13		"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3"
14	)
15	
16	// S3Store stores images in an S3-compatible bucket (Backblaze B2, etc.)
17	type S3Store struct {
18		client *s3.Client
19		bucket string
20	}
21	
22	func NewS3Store(endpoint, keyID, appKey, bucket string) (*S3Store, error) {
23		// Extract region from B2 endpoint (e.g. "https://s3.ca-east-006.backblazeb2.com" → "ca-east-006")
24		region := "us-east-1"
25		if parts := strings.Split(endpoint, "."); len(parts) >= 3 {
26			region = parts[1] // e.g. "ca-east-006"
27		}
28	
29		client := s3.New(s3.Options{
30			BaseEndpoint: aws.String(endpoint),
31			Region:       region,
32			Credentials:  credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(keyID, appKey, ""),
33			UsePathStyle: true,
34		})
35	
36		return &S3Store{client: client, bucket: bucket}, nil
37	}
38	
39	func (s *S3Store) Save(filename string, data io.Reader) error {
40		contentType := detectContentType(filename)
41		_, err := s.client.PutObject(context.Background(), &s3.PutObjectInput{
42			Bucket:      aws.String(s.bucket),
43			Key:         aws.String(filename),
44			Body:        data,
45			ContentType: aws.String(contentType),
46		})
47		return err
48	}
49	
50	func (s *S3Store) Open(filename string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
51		out, err := s.client.GetObject(context.Background(), &s3.GetObjectInput{
52			Bucket: aws.String(s.bucket),
53			Key:    aws.String(filename),
54		})
55		if err != nil {
56			return nil, err
57		}
58		return out.Body, nil
59	}

**Found the root cause!** All element IDs are `undefined`! 

```
hitIds: [undefined]  selectedIds.size: 1  will narrow: false
```

When `hit.id` is `undefined`, `hitIds = [undefined]`. Then `selectedIds = new Set([undefined])`. Since ALL elements have `id: undefined`, `selectedIds.has(el.id)` is `true` for every element — so **everything renders as selected**.

# Get draw IDs from page 65 and 66
echo "=== Page 65 draws ==="
curl -s 'https://taskai.cc/api/wiki/pages/65' -H "Authorization: ApiKey dummy" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys; print('need auth')" 2>/dev/null

# Page 66: let me check
curl -s 'https://taskai.cc/draw/ve7lg0kdwf/data' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('ve7lg0kdwf:', len(d['scene']['elements']), 'elements, has id:', bool(d['scene']['elements'][0].get('id')))"

# Fix all drawings by fetching, adding IDs, and re-saving
for DRAW_ID in ubrjqlqzdy puqk8tzivd m35vd4hjw4 ve7lg0kdwf; do
  echo "--- Fixing $DRAW_ID ---"
  DATA=$(curl -s "https://taskai.cc/draw/$DRAW_ID/data")
  TITLE=$(echo "$DATA" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('title','Untitled'))")
  SCENE=$(echo "$DATA" | python3 -c "
import sys, json, random, string
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
scene = d['scene']
fixed = 0
for el in scene.get('elements', []):
    if not el.get('id'):
        el['id'] = ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))
        fixed += 1
print(json.dumps(scene))
sys.stderr.write(f'{fixed} elements fixed\n')
" 2>&1)
  # Extract stderr count
  FIXED=$(echo "$SCENE" | tail -1)
  SCENE_JSON=$(echo "$SCENE" | head -1)
  echo "  $FIXED"
  
  # Save back
  SAVE_BODY=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'title': '$TITLE', 'scene': json.loads('''$SCENE_JSON''')}))")
  RESULT=$(curl -s -X POST "https://taskai.cc/draw/$DRAW_ID/save" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$SAVE_BODY")
  echo "  Save result: $RESULT"
done

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fix missing element IDs in go-draw drawings on production."""
import json
import random
import string
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://taskai.cc"
DRAW_IDS = ["ubrjqlqzdy", "puqk8tzivd", "m35vd4hjw4", "ve7lg0kdwf"]

def gen_id():
    return ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=10))

for draw_id in DRAW_IDS:
    print(f"\n--- {draw_id} ---")
    # Fetch
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/draw/{draw_id}/data") as resp:
        data = json.loads(resp.read())

    title = data.get("title", "Untitled")
    scene = data.get("scene", {"version": 1, "elements": []})

    fixed = 0
    for el in scene.get("elements", []):
        if not el.get("id"):
            el["id"] = gen_id()
            fixed += 1

    print(f"  Title: {title}")
    print(f"  Elements: {len(scene.get('elements', []))}, fixed: {fixed}")

    if fixed == 0:
        print("  Already has IDs, skipping")
        continue

    # Save back
    payload = json.dumps({"title": title, "scene": scene}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{BASE}/draw/{draw_id}/save",
        data=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        result = json.loads(resp.read())
    print(f"  Save result: {result}")
